weapon: None mentioned (kerosene poured on the victim and set alight)
evidence_type: Dying declaration; medical evidence (doctor's endorsement); forensic report (FSL) on clothing residue; circumstantial evidence
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302; sentence not stated in this judgment
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction under IPC s.302 upheld
neutral_facts: On 29 December 1998, at about 5 p.m., the accused allegedly poured kerosene on the body of the victim, who was his wife, and set her on fire. Two persons immediately took the victim to a hospital, where a doctor treated her and informed the police station. A police sub-inspector went to the hospital and recorded a dying declaration. In it the victim stated that the accused often drank liquor, quarrelled with her and assaulted her when drunk. On the same day the accused had given her Rs. 200 for groceries and taken back Rs. 100 of it, so she bought groceries with the remaining Rs. 100. Later that day he returned, demanded the Rs. 100 back and asked her to return the groceries. When she refused, he became angry, tied her hands, poured kerosene on her body and set her ablaze. The victim died of the burn injuries on 19 January 1999. The treating doctor endorsed that the victim was in a fit mental condition to depose before the police. A Forensic Science Laboratory report found kerosene residue on the victim's brassiere, saree and petticoat. The two persons who took the victim to hospital turned hostile during their testimony. No second dying declaration was recorded before a Magistrate. The accused offered no explanation for the kerosene found on the victim's clothing, and no suggestion of suicide or accident was put forward.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from burn injuries sustained after kerosene was poured and set alight (death on 19.1.1999)
motive: alleged: dispute over Rs. 100 the accused demanded back from the victim after she had spent the money on groceries
key_evidence_accepted: Dying declaration recorded by PW-13 and endorsed by PW-5 as to fit mental condition; FSL report (Exhibit P-25) showing kerosene residue on brassiere, saree and petticoat; absence of any explanation by the accused for the kerosene
witness_credibility: Witnesses who took the victim to hospital were hostile, but the court held this did not help the accused; the dying declaration and circumstantial evidence were treated as reliable
trial_duration: offence: 29.12.1998; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 03.11.2003; Supreme Court: April 19, 2011
legal_representation: Accused: Ram Lal Roy; State (respondent): Gurudatta Ankolekar, Azeem Kalebudde, V.N. Raghuparthy
investigation_status: Police recorded dying declaration; FSL report obtained (Exhibit P-25); case tried and conviction under s.302 IPC followed
procedural_irregularity: Investigating officer did not attempt to have the second dying declaration recorded by a Magistrate; the court said this would have been better but did not vitiate the dying declaration
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302 IPC; High Court (Criminal Appeal No. 460 of 2000, 03.11.2003): conviction upheld; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
defence_argument: Investigating officer failed to get the second dying declaration recorded by a Magistrate
legal_principle_applied: A dying declaration can be the sole basis for conviction if it is good; corroboration from circumstances (kerosene residue on clothing, no explanation by accused) and hostile witnesses do not defeat proof
